coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed meaningfully and non-overlappingly: openspec decomposed compound ACs into atomic, machine-verifiable checks and added structural coverage (.gitignore, src/, explicit dep lists); speckit hardened content specificity (defineConfig import constraint, 'no output' qualifier on tsc, negative SDK assertion, reordering). The negative Skyscanner/RapidAPI SDK assertion is a net-new correctness guard that neither predecessor flagged — good speckit initiative. However, speckit closed only 2 of the 4 substantive gaps flagged by the prior coordinator review: (1) missing_src_entry_point_ac remains unaddressed — src/ directory existing does not prove a usable scaffold; a src/index.ts stub AC is still absent. (2) tsconfig_moduleResolution_not_asserted remains unaddressed — with module: CommonJS and tsx in dev deps, an explicit moduleResolution: node AC would eliminate a latent tsc failure vector on path imports. (3) express_wiring_not_verified is partially mitigated by the tsc --noEmit clean AC, but the absence of a smoke-test import or listening-server check means a broken express wire could pass all current ACs. The vitest.config.ts gap is now mostly closed (defineConfig import required) but the test include glob and environment (node vs jsdom) remain unspecified — acceptable given the 'no test files is passing' allowance, but worth noting. Story is actionable as-is given the strong executable gates, but the three residual gaps warrant one more targeted speckit pass before locking.

stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI. The client must: (1) export a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor accepts { apiKey: string }; if apiKey is omitted, fall back to the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable — throw a descriptive Error if neither is present; (2) implement searchFlights(params: SearchParams): Promise<FlightResult[]> using the Node.js 18+ global fetch (no third-party HTTP library); (3) export TypeScript interfaces SearchParams { origin: string; destination: string; date: string; adults?: number } and FlightResult { price: number; currency: string; airline: string; departure: string; arrival: string; duration: number; stops: number }; (4) throw on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, including the status code in the message; (5) throw a descriptive parse error when the response body does not match the expected shape. Also create src/skyscanner/client.test.ts with vitest tests that mock the global fetch — no real network calls.
acceptanceCriteria: src/skyscanner/client.ts exports a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor signature is constructor({ apiKey }: { apiKey?: string })
SearchParams interface is exported with exactly: origin: string, destination: string, date: string, adults?: number
FlightResult interface is exported with exactly: price: number, currency: string, airline: string, departure: string, arrival: string, duration: number, stops: number
searchFlights uses the Node.js global fetch exclusively — no axios, node-fetch, or other HTTP dependency imported
When no apiKey is passed to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is unset, constructing SkyscannerClient throws an Error whose message references the missing key
When the API returns a 4xx or 5xx status, searchFlights rejects with an Error that includes the HTTP status code
When the API response body is malformed or missing expected fields, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error

client.test.ts contains at least 5 vitest tests, each using a mocked fetch (vi.stubGlobal or equivalent) with afterEach fetch restoration, covering: (a) correct RapidAPI URL and header construction, (b) successful response parsed into FlightResult[], (c) HTTP 4xx rejection with status code in error message, (d) missing API key constructor error, (e) malformed/missing-fields response body rejects with a parse/validation error
tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no type errors
vitest run exits 0 with all tests passing
The apiKey is stored as a private field (private or # prefix) on the SkyscannerClient instance and is not publicly readable
When apiKey is passed as an empty string ('') to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the same missing-key Error as when apiKey is omitted entirely
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is set to an empty string in the environment and no apiKey is provided to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the missing-key Error
When an apiKey is provided to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY is also set in the environment, the constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence
The Error thrown by searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx does not include the apiKey value anywhere in its message string

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Exemplary two-agent collaboration with clean division of labor. openspec correctly established the TypeScript contract layer (constructor signature, exact interface shapes, fetch-only constraint, env-var fallback, error taxonomy). speckit added non-overlapping security and correctness hardening: private field enforcement, empty-string equivalence for constructor and env-var, afterEach fetch restoration, constructor-arg precedence over env-var, and the security constraint that apiKey must never appear in error message strings. The AC-7/AC-8 test gap (malformed-response behavior specified but not tested) was correctly identified and closed by speckit (test case (e) added, count raised 4→5). Final 15 ACs are independently verifiable and non-overlapping. Blocked on two unresolved external knowledge gaps: (1) the RapidAPI host, path, and required header names are never specified — AC-8 test case (a) asserts 'correct RapidAPI URL and header construction' but an implementor cannot write a meaningful assertion against an unknown endpoint contract; this is BUILD-BLOCKING; (2) the `date` field in SearchParams carries no format constraint — YYYY-MM-DD validation may or may not be in scope for this story and must be decided before implementation starts. Both gaps were surfaced by speckit and are external knowledge failures, not spec failures.
flags: BLOCKING: RapidAPI endpoint URL (host + path) and required header names are unspecified — AC-8 test case (a) cannot be written as a meaningful assertion without this; requires human decision on expected host/path/header contract before story is buildable
NEEDS_DECISION: `date` field in SearchParams has no format constraint — team must decide if YYYY-MM-DD parsing/validation belongs in this story or a follow-on before implementation starts

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point with formatted table output
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner-client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table with columns: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Column widths are determined by the widest value in each column (including the header). A separator row of hyphen characters must appear between the header and data rows. Price is right-aligned and prefixed with the currency symbol returned by the API (default £ if absent); all other columns are left-aligned. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1. Create `src/cli.test.ts` covering argument validation, successful render, empty-result render, missing env var, and error handling using vitest with `SkyscannerClient` mocked at the module boundary. The compiled output must be invokable as `node dist/cli.js ...` after `tsc`; `tsconfig.json` must have `outDir` set to `dist` and emit CommonJS-compatible output.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/cli.ts` exists and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors
`tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` to `dist` and emits a module format compatible with `node dist/cli.js` invocation (CommonJS or ESM with .mjs extension consistently applied)
Flags `--from`, `--to`, and `--date` are all required; if any is absent the CLI prints a usage hint to stderr (showing correct flag names) and exits with code 2
The `--date` flag value must match the pattern `YYYY-MM-DD`; a value that does not match this format causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message written to stderr before any network call is made
Optional `--adults` flag defaults to 1 when omitted; a non-integer value, a value ≤ 0, or a non-numeric string causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message to stderr
The parsed `adults` value is forwarded as an argument to `SkyscannerClient.searchFlights` — the flag is not silently dropped
If `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var is unset or empty, CLI prints 'Error: RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is required' to stderr and exits 1 before making any network call

When `searchFlights` resolves with one or more results, stdout contains: (a) a header row with columns Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops; (b) a separator row of hyphen characters whose width matches each column exactly; (c) one data row per result; all columns padded to the width of the widest value in that column (including the header label)
All columns except Price are left-aligned within their padded width; the Price column is right-aligned within its padded width
Price column values are prefixed with the currency symbol from the API response; if the API response omits a currency symbol, £ is used as the fallback
When `searchFlights` resolves with an empty array, stdout contains exactly the line `No flights found.` and process exits 0
When `searchFlights` rejects, the error message is written to stderr and process exits 1; stdout is empty

`src/cli.test.ts` contains at least 8 passing vitest tests covering: missing --from, missing --to, missing --date, invalid --adults value, missing RAPIDAPI_KEY env var, table rendered correctly for valid multi-row results (verify separator row present and column alignment), empty-array result renders 'No flights found.', and error path (client throws)
`vitest run` exits 0 with all tests green
No runtime dependency other than Node built-ins and packages already in `package.json` (from SKY-001/SKY-002) is added

specification.coordinatorNotes: Two targeted gaps survived the prior speckit pass: (1) TEST_GAP — AC-6 specifies RAPIDAPI_KEY-absent behavior (exit 1, stderr message, no network call) but AC-11's 7-test enumeration does not include this path; speckit should add it as test case (f) and bump the count to 8; (2) AC_NOTE_MISMATCH — openspec notes reference a shebang/chmod+x requirement never promoted to a formal AC; speckit should either add it as an AC or explicitly mark it out of scope for this story. No structural re-elaboration needed — these are narrow, surgical additions to an otherwise complete spec.

agentContributions.notes: Added date-format validation AC (YYYY-MM-DD), clarified column alignment (left for all non-Price columns), upgraded minimum test count from 7 to 8 to include the RAPIDAPI_KEY missing scenario, and tightened separator-row wording to 'hyphen characters' to remove ambiguity. No split recommended — implementation and tests are too tightly coupled to separate usefully.

stories.title: Build Express REST API with /health, /search, /cheapest, and static dashboard endpoints
stories.description: Create src/server.ts — an Express HTTP server that exposes: (1) GET /health → { status: 'ok', uptime: number }, (2) GET /search?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01&adults=1 → { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string }, (3) GET /cheapest?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01 → the single cheapest FlightResult or 404 JSON { error: string } if none found, (4) GET / → serves src/public/index.html. Server reads PORT from env (default 3000); reads RAPIDAPI_KEY from env and passes to SkyscannerClient. If RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at startup all API routes (/search, /cheapest) return 503 { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; /health and / are never gated. The listen() call must be guarded so importing `app` in tests does not bind a port. Add 'start' script in package.json pointing to 'node dist/server.js'. Install supertest and @types/supertest. Create src/server.test.ts using vitest + supertest with at least 8 tests covering the scenarios in acceptance criteria. Depends on SKY-002 (SkyscannerClient and FlightResult type must exist before this story is started).
acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) separately from the `listen()` call so supertest can import it without binding a port

The `listen()` call in src/server.ts is guarded by `import { pathToFileURL } from 'url'` and the condition `if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)` (ESM output) or `if (require.main === module)` (CJS output) — the guard form must match the tsup output format so that `vitest run` never binds a port
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body matching { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> }
GET /health returns HTTP 200 regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is set or absent — the health endpoint is never gated by API key presence
GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type matching text/html and response body equal to the contents of src/public/index.html — this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY
src/public/index.html exists and contains valid HTML (at minimum a non-empty file with an <html> root element)

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is absent on GET /search, the request succeeds (HTTP 200) with a default value of 1 passed to SkyscannerClient — `adults` is optional, not required
When the `adults` query param is present but non-numeric (e.g. 'abc', ''), GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

GET /cheapest with valid required query params (from, to, date) returns HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult whose `price` field is less than or equal to the `price` field of every FlightResult returned by SkyscannerClient for the same route/date (validated against a mocked client response); if `adults` is supplied it is forwarded, if absent it defaults to 1
GET /cheapest returns HTTP 404 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } when SkyscannerClient returns an empty array for the given route/date
GET /cheapest missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialisation, a single middleware (or equivalent) short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected and return their normal responses

When SkyscannerClient throws an error during a /search or /cheapest request (e.g. network failure, upstream 5xx), the server returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } and does not crash or emit an unhandled promise rejection

The `searchedAt` field in the GET /search response is an ISO-8601 datetime string reflecting the time of the request (not a hardcoded value); successive requests separated by at least 1 ms return distinct values

The FlightResult type used in src/server.ts is imported from the SKY-002 type export (e.g. src/skyscanner-client.ts) and not redeclared inline — type definitions must not diverge between the client and server layers
package.json contains a 'start' script with value 'node dist/server.js'
package.json contains a 'build' script (tsup or equivalent) that produces dist/server.js such that `npm run build && npm run start` successfully starts the server and GET /health returns HTTP 200
supertest and @types/supertest are listed in package.json devDependencies

src/server.test.ts contains at least 8 vitest tests, each covering a distinct scenario from the criteria above, with SkyscannerClient mocked (vi.mock or equivalent) so no real HTTP calls are made during `vitest run`
`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no type errors
`vitest run` exits 0 with all tests passing

specification.coordinatorNotes: One BLOCKING gap survived both prior agent passes: the server URL query params use `from`/`to` while SkyscannerClient.SearchParams uses `origin`/`destination` — no AC requires or tests this mapping translation, meaning a conforming implementation will silently fail on every /search and /cheapest request at runtime. speckit should: (1) add an explicit AC requiring the server to map from→origin and to→destination when calling SkyscannerClient; (2) add a corresponding test to the AC-20 test enumeration; (3) make an explicit scope decision on CORS headers and query-injection hardening — either add ACs or formally defer to a follow-on story with a note in the spec. No openspec re-run needed; the structural elaboration is complete.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: speckit added genuine correctness value: the listen() guard AC (app export alone is insufficient — a bare import during vitest will still bind a port without the guard), FlightResult type-import AC (enforces SKY-002 dependency and prevents silent type drift between layers), non-numeric adults → 400 AC (closes a validation gap), searchedAt distinctness tightened to '1 ms apart', and 503 scope correctly narrowed to API routes only with /health and / explicitly unaffected. The build script AC is a practical addition. Final 23 ACs are well-formed and non-overlapping. However, the BLOCKING gap called out explicitly in the coordinator notes was NOT resolved by speckit: the server URL query params use `from`/`to` while SkyscannerClient.SearchParams uses `origin`/`destination` — no AC requires this mapping translation to be implemented or tested. An implementor following the ACs as written can pass all 8 mandated tests while forwarding `from` directly into a `from` key on SearchParams, which the client will silently ignore or reject at runtime. Every /search and /cheapest request will fail in production. This translation must be added as an explicit AC with a corresponding test before the story is buildable. The CORS/security-headers deferral was noted but no explicit scope decision was recorded.
flags: BLOCKING: No AC requires or tests the from→origin / to→destination parameter mapping between URL query params and SkyscannerClient.SearchParams — this translation is a runtime correctness requirement; without it every /search and /cheapest call will silently forward wrong keys; must be added as an AC with a corresponding test before story is buildable
